mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Commercial Registry Extract of each direct shareholder entity (or the original Registration Certificate of the founder entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the country of origin (for Korea-origin entities, the district court registry office under the Supreme Court of Korea)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: certification by the designated Competent Authority in the document's country of origin; no Korean consulate step. Consular Legalization (only for non-Apostille countries): local notarization, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication in the country of origin, then legalization by the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in that country. These two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of No Tax Objection from the jurisdiction of each corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority or company registry / secretary of state in the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Use either the Hague Apostille path or the Korean consular legalization path, whichever applies to the country of origin; the parallel path structure is exactly as set out for the Certificate of Incorporation, and the two alternatives cannot be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the Korea formation and appointing the local representative and AML/KYC submission agents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate parent or sponsor, notarized locally and counter-signed by the company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for member states; for non-member states, local notarization, foreign ministry legalization, then legalization by the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in the issuing state; never use apostille and consular legalization together on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (memorandum and articles) of the Yuhan Hoesa being incorporated, executed by the founding shareholders and certified for filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean counsel and founding shareholders, filed with the district court registration office in the jurisdiction of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean domestic filing does not require consular or apostille treatment; if the signed Articles must be presented abroad, they must be notarized in Korea and then authenticated either by Korean Apostille (if destination is an Apostille state) or by Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by legalization at the destination consulate (if destination is a non-Apostille state).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (original) of the principal shareholder/founder covering account conduct, expected transactional volumes, and no adverse banking history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the beneficial owner or founding shareholder, signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer notarization followed by the single applicable channel: Hague Apostille for member states, or Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization for non-member states; the two channels are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to permitting any shareholder action, screen every natural-person UBO, director, representative, and signatory against the Republic of Korea's financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK OFSI Consolidated List, and all Ministry of Economy and Finance financial sanctions designations. Conduct PEP checks for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, and perform adverse media and source-of-wealth reviews. Repeat screening at least every 90 days, upon any ownership or signature change, and before each payment retry that touches a bank rail. All positive matches must be cleared in writing by the AML compliance officer and filed with KoFIU under the statutory suspicious transaction reporting obligation where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS, https://www.iros.go.kr) company name clearance and name reservation module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in Hangul, and the Korean district court registration office will not register a pure English or Chinese-character name as the primary legal name. English Romanization is used for tax invoices, bank references, and international contracts and must follow the National Institute of Korean Language loanword orthography doctrine. The four-tier naming formula is: distinctive brand element, business activity descriptor, optional geographic or market descriptor, and the obligatory Yuhan Hoesa suffix. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name pursuing the same or substantially similar business purpose.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, obtain the IROS rejection notice and confirm the identical or confusingly similar business purpose criterion. The applicant has 14 days to petition the district court registrar under the Commercial Registration Rules, explaining the distinguishing brand and business descriptors. In the alternative, file a reconsideration request with the registration officer. If the reconsideration is denied, initiate a civil interlocutory objection before the competent district court within 30 days of service. Attach the original clearance search, proposed Hangul name, English transliteration, precise business purpose, and any ministerial approval obtained for a sensitive token. The registry must rule on the written record without requiring an oral hearing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are tolerated by the Korean district court for registration only if the service provider can produce a valid lease and the location is not a mere letterbox. For a payroll SaaS company, the National Tax Service expects a productive physical location during VAT and payroll tax registration, and Korean banks under KoFIU CDD rules will almost always reject a bank account when the registered address is a virtual mailbox only. Therefore, a staffed serviced office or shared physical suite with a designated local agent and payroll/HR processing infrastructure is strongly recommended. A pure virtual office with no local presence should be treated as high-risk for banking onboarding and tax audit rejection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: [1] mismatch between registered address and actual operational address; [2] no local employee or designated agent physically present; [3] no business signage; [4] frequent address changes; [5] absence of lease documentation; [6] negligible local payroll; [7] purely digital operation with no verifiable business equipment. Quantified risk: for a newly registered IT/HR SaaS entity relying on virtual office only, the National Tax Service and municipal registry carry out unannounced compliance visits at an estimated 45-60% likelihood during the first year; a staffed physical serviced office reduces this estimated likelihood to 5-10%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 (Yuhan Hoesa), read together with the Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 15466, as amended) and Article 103 of the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act; foreign investment and foreign exchange obligations under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act apply to non-resident members.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court exercising jurisdiction over the registered office (in Seoul: Seoul Central District Court Registration Division), operating through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean-language court form) plus the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the bank deposit balance certificate for paid-up contribution units.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa; the articles may fix the total capital in any amount. However, each member must fully pay the subscribed contribution amount in cash or in-kind before the incorporation registration is filed, and the bank must issue a deposit balance certificate evidencing full payment. Korean law does not require a blocked escrow account, but the company should treat the deposit as restricted until the registry issues the incorporation certificate. Non-resident members may subscribe and pay, subject to foreign exchange bank declarations and anti-money-laundering identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LLC)

Date: [●]
Place: [●]
Present: [●], sole director/first director of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), duly appointed by the unanimous written consent of the initial members.

WHEREAS the initial members have subscribed for the entire initial contribution units of the Company and have agreed to the amounts, payment method and governance provisions contained in the Articles of Incorporation; and

WHEREAS the director(s) must take immediately necessary measures to complete the statutory incorporation, open bank accounts, adopt a registered office, appoint statutory officers and authorize filings so that the Company can lawfully commence its payroll automation and staff compliance software business.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. Capital Subscription and Payment. The subscription to the full initial capital of KRW [●], divided into [●] contribution units with a contribution value of KRW [●] per unit, is ratified and accepted. The representative director is instructed to verify that each member has paid the full contribution amount into a corporate temporary account and to present the bank deposit balance certificate and any in-kind valuation report to the Registration Division of the competent District Court as required by Article 287-7 of the Commercial Act.

2. Statutory Officer Appointments. [Name], [passport number], is appointed as representative director (sole director/chief executive officer), and [Name] is appointed as auditor/reviewer, to hold office until the first ordinary members' meeting or earlier removal in accordance with the Articles. Each appointee accepts the office and consents in writing to act and to be registered.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [full address in the Republic of Korea]. The representative director is authorized to execute the lease agreement, obtain the landlord's consent, lodge the lease with the court registry, and maintain the office as the place where statutory notices and process may be served.

4. Banking Authorization. The representative director is authorized to open corporate bank accounts with one or more commercial banks, to issue wire and direct debit instructions, to execute banking mandates, and to designate authorized signatories. The bank mandate shall require joint authorization for any single payment exceeding KRW [●] or any use of SWIFT or direct debit rails exceeding that threshold.

5. Regulatory Filings. The representative director is directed to prepare, file and pursue the application for incorporation registration with the competent District Court; to complete business registration with the National Tax Service; to obtain corporate seal and tax invoice certificates; and to register the Company with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance for each employee, in compliance with Korean law.

6. Delegation and Completion. All directors and the appointed auditor may delegate to legal counsel and licensed agents any powers necessary to cure formal deficiencies, pay fees, collect certified copies and effect supplementary filings, provided the delegation is in writing. This resolution is fully effective from the date of adoption until the Company has completed all post-incorporation registrations.

ADOPTED this [●] day of [●], [Year], by the signature of the initial director(s).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea — electronic portal at HomeTax (https://hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the domestic Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) with non-resident shareholders: (1) register with the Korean Commercial Court registry to obtain the corporate seal and certificate of incorporation; (2) within 20 days of business commencement, submit a Corporate Business Registration Application to the local NTS district tax office through the HomeTax portal, attaching the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, head office lease contract, and passport copies of foreign ultimate beneficial owners; (3) the NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number that serves as the VAT identification number and corporate TIN; (4) the representative director must also activate the e-invoice certificate for electronic tax invoice issuance. For a foreign non-resident entity without a domestic establishment supplying SaaS or payroll automation services to Korean buyers, the foreign supplier must register through the HomeTax 'Foreign Business Operator' module using its home-country tax ID, a Korean agent or representative, and submit an application for a foreign-registrant VAT ID; no domestic corporation registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea applies an entity-level mandatory corporate income tax and VAT system; there is no check-the-box election and no tax consolidation for unrelated domestic subsidiaries. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Korean International Tax Adjustment Act apply for instrument/entity mismatches, but a Korean LLC may not elect pass-through status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 — no de minimis exemption. Both domestic and foreign suppliers of taxable goods/services, including cloud-based payroll automation SaaS, are required to register for VAT from the date of commencing business. For small traders, a simplified taxpayer regime may apply for annual taxable supplies below KRW 80,000,000, but registration itself remains compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea mandates electronic tax invoices through the HomeTax e-invoice system. All taxpayers with annual prior-year turnover exceeding KRW 80,000,000 must issue e-invoices digitally through the NTS API within 1 day for B2B transactions and 5 days for B2C transactions; the system performs real-time transmission, validates the integrated tax invoice identification number, and applies cryptographic anti-fraud stamping. Taxpayers under the threshold may still issue fallback invoices but must migrate to e-invoices when turnover exceeds KRW 80,000,000 in the preceding year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act and its Enforcement Decree, a supplier can claim zero-rated VAT on: (i) goods exported from Korea via the Korea Customs Service; (ii) services rendered to foreign non-resident businesses or foreign individuals, including international transport and digital services (SaaS, payroll automation) that are used or consumed wholly outside Korea; and (iii) services physically performed outside Korea. The supplier must hold written contracts identifying the foreign buyer, a zero-rated e-invoice, bank clearing evidence of foreign-currency receipt or SWIFT credit, and, where relevant, network/server logs proving the service was not used in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Korea Customs Service 'Export Declaration' / 'Cargo Clearance Report' proving physical shipment)
Commercial invoice and packing list with the foreign buyer's full name, address, and foreign tax identification number
Bill of lading (B/L) or air waybill (AWB) evidencing the goods left Korean territory and arrived in the destination country

Foreign exchange bank certificate (equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate) issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank showing receipt of the export price in foreign currency, or SWIFT statement showing final credit
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued to the foreign purchaser and transmitted via the HomeTax e-invoice portal, together with the NTS real-time transmission record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will match the zero-rated return with the customs export declaration, e-invoice transmission, and SWIFT credit history. If export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days or the zero-rating substantiation bundle is incomplete or forged, the NTS retroactively assesses 10% VAT on the export value, disallows associated input VAT credits, and imposes understatement penalties (typically 10%–40% of the omitted tax) plus statutory late-payment surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes. In cases of fraudulent export evidence, the responsible parties may be criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, and the assessment period is extended to 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea, as executing foreign exchange control agency under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and Korea Customs Service for export settlement enforcement
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a substantially open but regulated convertibility regime. Current account transactions, including software subscription fees, license royalties, management fees, and cross-border payroll-related expenses, are generally free from prior approval, but must be executed through a domestic foreign exchange bank and reported to Bank of Korea and Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Capital account transactions are more controlled. An inbound equity investment, shareholder loan, or capital deposit from a non-resident owner triggers reporting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; a foreign equity investment in a Yuhan Hoesa may also need a report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Profit remittance is allowed only after the Korean entity can evidence that corporate tax has been paid or withheld, that no outstanding customs or tax arrears exist, and that board approval has authorized the dividend; the bank then records the payment with an FX purpose code. The Korean won is not freely deliverable offshore for settlement in non-designated banking channels, and settlement timing differences can create liquidity friction. Export receipts are subject to statutory repatriation deadlines. Therefore, the treasury must maintain accurate FEIS records, isolate capital account injections, and keep documented current-account contracts to preserve full won convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods exports, all foreign currency export proceeds must be repatriated through a certified Korean foreign exchange bank within 18 months of the export declaration date unless an extension is approved by the bank or relevant authority; for service exports by the payroll SaaS company, collection may follow the approved service-export settlement timeline and must still be received in full. The mandatory receipt ratio is 100% of the invoiced export value; there is no forced conversion percentage to Korean won, but the proceeds must be surrendered to the Korean banking system through a foreign currency account or KRW conversion and reported through FEIS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs without a Korean banking license or e-money/funds-transfer authorization under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act are not viable as a primary treasury or corporate bank account. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires foreign-exchange business and settlement transactions to flow through a domestic foreign-exchange bank, and Korean AML rules require a local regulated identifier, real-name verification, and FEIS reporting. A licensed offshore EMI may only be used as an ancillary collection channel for small international payroll SaaS subscription receipts, and only if it routes actual settlement to the Korean Tier-1 bank account. Feasibility rating: Low for statutory capital, escrow, FX, or clearing functions; conditional Medium as a non-core receivables gateway.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Korean Tier-1 bank will generally require at least one officer or statutory representative director of the Yuhan Hoesa to attend an in-branch KYC interview with original passport, corporate seal or equivalent authentication, business registration certificate, certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, beneficial ownership declaration, and financial statements. Pure remote account opening for a foreign-owned Korean LLC is rarely granted; a proxy opening is possible only if the bank approves a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, the proxy identity is verified by video call, and all corporate documents are certified by Korean counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO opacity and group structure without clear Korean economic substance can trigger a front-company or conduit-company red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full certified corporate registry file of the Yuhan Hoesa, South Korean business registration certificate, certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, beneficial ownership declaration to the ultimate individual shareholders, notarized English-Korean translations, audited financial statements, office lease, employee payroll records, tax clearance certificates, and a business plan demonstrating a live payroll automation platform with local technical and sales substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-source initial capital and equity funding without a visible source-of-wealth trail can trigger a source-of-funds rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Equity subscription agreement, board minutes approving the capital contribution, inward wire instruction with FEIS purpose code, source-of-wealth dossier for each subscribing shareholder, shareholder bank statements and tax returns, CPA or auditor capital verification letter, and foreign investment report confirmation submitted at the foreign exchange bank or KOTRA when applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, fraudulent-economy jurisdiction, or negative-media hits on UBOs and commercial counterparties can trigger enhanced due diligence or account termination.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and residence proof for every UBO and statutory officer, signed PEP and sanctions declaration, third-party screening reports from a reputable vendor, identity and citizenship documentation, board-approved compliance attestation, explanatory counsel letter for each hit, and a register of commercial counterparties with invoice-level rationale for the payroll SaaS business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume third-party salary and payroll disbursements for external clients can create mule-account or layering risk even though the company is a payroll SaaS vendor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client payroll and software service agreements, end-client AML/KYC due diligence files, payroll registers tying each beneficiary to active employment or contractor records, information security certificates such as ISO 27001 or Korean ISMS certification, audit logs from the payroll engine, data sub-processor list, and written confirmation that client funds are never commingled with Yuhan Hoesa operating funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from a foreign shareholder should be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the funding institution to the Yuhan Hoesa's beneficiary account at a Korean Tier-1 bank, with the remittance purpose code stated as capital contribution or foreign equity investment under the Foreign Exchange Information System rules and, if a non-resident shareholder seeks protected foreign-invested status, a prior report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through the delegated bank or KOTRA. The bank will require the signed capital subscription agreement, board resolution, UBO identification, source of wealth, and evidence of no prohibited jurisdiction. After credit, the Korean bank issues the FEIS confirmation and the company's external auditor verifies paid-in capital for statutory reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operating and payroll SaaS trade disbursements should be cleared through the Korean foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 for foreign contractors, software licensing, marketing, recruitment, and tax-withheld service fees; commercial letters of credit and documentary collections can be used for physical software or dongle/license kit deliveries, but are not the default for SaaS payroll automations. Domestic payroll can be disbursed via Korean direct debit/ACH bank files; each outbound transfer must be backed by an underlying contract, valid invoice, withholding tax documentation where required, and automatic FEIS reporting by the bank, with beneficial ownership and counterparty screening completed before instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forwards up to 12 months for documented payroll, software subscription, and vendor payment cash-flow exposure, executed through the Korean Tier-1 bank on an underlying transaction basis

Bank-approved non-deliverable forwards for KRW risk only when the treasury can prove genuine current-account exposure and no speculative intent; onshore NDF use is tightly constrained and must be documented in the hedging policy

Cross-currency interest rate swaps or simple FX swaps for balance-sheet hedging of foreign-currency capital, shareholder loans, or long-term licensing receivables, subject to FEIS reporting, board approval, and tenor matching with the underlying exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, March 31 of the following year. An automatic one-month extension is available on timely application; companies with overseas business may obtain further extension of up to 3 months from the District Tax Office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing/underreporting: 20% penalty on unpaid corporate tax (40% in cases of willful concealment); daily overdue surtax of 0.022% per day on unpaid tax; potential criminal indictment for fraudulent returns; administrative collection measures, including seizure of bank accounts and business licenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax on Corporate Income (Jijbangsode-dae-se)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government (si/gun/gu) and Ministry of the Interior and Safety; collected simultaneously with the NTS return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the corporate income tax return (within 3 months after fiscal year-end); pre-payments for sizable entities are due March 31 and September 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local income tax surtax incurs a 3% deficiency penalty plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day until payment; prolonged delinquency triggers compulsory collection, property attachment, and registered-disgrace under local tax laws.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and External Auditor's Report (for companies subject to statutory audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer (DART) electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end, and no later than 15 days after the annual general meeting approving the financial statements; for a December year-end, the full filing chain must be completed by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, failure to file the audit report leads to administrative fines up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 38,000), correction orders, designation of a supervising CPA firm, disciplinary sanctions against the auditor, and for repeated violations, suspension of directors or criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Report (if any foreign investor holds 10% or more of quotas or has de facto control)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year (for a calendar-year company, on or before January 31) or as otherwise prescribed in the foreign investment award.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 1 million (approximately USD 760) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and loss or clawback of tax and FX incentives attached to the foreign-invested enterprise status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa must engage an independent licensed CPA to perform a statutory audit if: (i) total assets at the preceding fiscal year-end are at least KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.1 million); or (ii) total annual operating revenue is at least KRW 100 billion (approx. USD 76 million); or (iii) the average number of employees is at least 300; or (iv) the company is a listed/public securities issuer regardless of size. The Financial Services Commission may designate additional entities as subject to audit on an industry or risk basis. Companies not crossing these quantitative thresholds are generally free from mandatory external audit, but banks, tax authorities or financiers may still require audited financial statements as a contractual or regulatory condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board) is mandatory for entities required to adopt K-IFRS, including securities-listed companies and large unlisted groups. Non-public enterprises that are not required to apply K-IFRS may prepare financial statements under Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) or K-IFRS for SMEs, subject to consistency and disclosure requirements. All accounts must be expressed in Korean won and maintained in the Korean language.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a single annual UBO confirmation filing for private limited companies. However, a Yuhan Hoesa is required to maintain a current register of members/quota-holders at its registered office, and any transfer of membership quotas, change of directors, or amendment of the articles of incorporation must be entered in the register and, where relevant, registered with the competent Court Registry of Registration (Commercial Registration) within 30 days of the occurrence of the change. On an event-driven basis, the company must keep identification evidence of ultimate beneficial owners for Korea's Anti-Money Laundering and Real Name Financial Transactions regimes, and must answer lawful inspection requests from the Financial Intelligence Unit and the NTS.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors
Minute Book of Members' and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for a licensed professional corporate service provider covering a Seoul/Incheon registered office, mail forwarding, statutory register upkeep, and calendar management; USD 500 - USD 1,200 per annum in other provinces.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 30,000 per annum for a certified external audit, tailored to asset scale, complexity of payroll SaaS revenue recognition, use of K-IFRS, and transfer pricing exposure; small enterprises that just cross the audit threshold typically pay the lower end.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea operates a progressive CIT schedule: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 21% between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion. Applicable incentives include the R&D tax credit (up to 20-40% of qualifying R&D expenditure), the Foreign Investment Promotion Act free-zone regime (100% corporate and local income tax exemption for 5 years with 50% reduction for an additional 2 years for eligible high-tech foreign investment), the headquarters support tax credit, and the International Finance Corporation special cases. No patent box regime exists, but the IP-derived income upon transfer or licensing may qualify for capital gains tax deferral under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준및세액신고서) via Home Tax Service (HTS / 홈택스) or National Tax Service e-filing portal; returns must be submitted to the competent regional tax office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending December 31, the deadline is March 31. If the close of the fiscal year is other than December 31, the deadline is the last day of the third month following the fiscal-year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income (total revenue from all business sources, including deemed revenue from foreign subsidiaries and controlled transactions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure that all Korean-source revenue, including SaaS subscription fees received from Korean customers through cross-border digital delivery, is fully reported. Adjustments must be made for any revenue attributable to a Korean permanent establishment (PE) if the non-resident entity has a dependent agent or fixed place of business in Korea. Failure to report digital cross-border revenue may trigger the VAT or Corporate Tax Act deemed revenue provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions (ordinary and necessary business expenses, depreciation, amortization, and allowable reserves).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers operating through a Korean branch may deduct expenses directly attributable to the PE, including intercompany management fees and software development costs, provided they are arm's length, documented, and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing records. Deductions for royalties paid to a foreign head office are restricted unless a valid cost-sharing arrangement is in place and the royalty is at arm's length. Excess deductions claimed by a non-resident without appropriate documentation will be disallowed and may trigger the 10% aggressive tax penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before special deductions and loss carryforward (computed after prior-year net operating losses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a PE must compute Korean-source taxable income independently from head-office worldwide income. Transfer pricing adjustments are applied here; if a taxpayer fails to file the Transfer Pricing Adjustment Statement (Form 43-1), tax authority may impose an upward adjustment on the deemed arm's-length income. Any inconsistent loss utilization by non-resident entities without a valid PE position will be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total corporate tax calculation after progressive rate application, additional income taxes (including deemed taxes), and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must apply the same progressive rates as domestic corporations on the PE taxable income. Treaty non-discrimination provisions do not override the domestic rate schedule. Other corporate taxes, such as the Corporate Tax for Local Income Tax (local surtax of 10% of corporate tax), must be reported on the same return. Non-resident entities claiming a tax credit must attach the appropriate Treaty-based Reduced Rate/Waiver certificate (Form 23) and prove beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable after credits, prepayments, and withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident entity has a PE and derives only Korean-source business profits, final tax is settled after deducting interim tax prepayments and any withholding tax on non-business Korean-source income. For non-residents without a PE, profits from digital services are not subject to corporate income tax unless attributable to a PE; however, the tax authority closely scrutinizes appointment of dependent agents and solicitation of contracts through a fixed place to pierce the no-PE claim. Any underpayment of tax exceeding 30% of the tax due is subject to 100% of the unpaid tax plus 0.025% per day under-reporting interest penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual corporate return by the statutory deadline: a penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax amount; failure to pay the correct amount: 10% of the underpaid amount; if the underpayment is due to dishonest intent or gross negligence, a 30% penalty. Additionally, daily overdue interest of 0.025% (approximately 9.125% annualized) applies to unpaid tax from the due date. If a taxpayer knowingly submits a fraudulent return in excess of KRW 1 billion in tax evaded, the criminal sanction is imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 200 million. Imprisonment is mandatory for evasion exceeding KRW 1 billion. For failure to maintain or submit transfer pricing documentation, the National Tax Service may impose a penalty of up to KRW 10 million per metric, temporarily detain financial records, and issue administrative forfeiture.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate income tax on dividend income plus 2% local income tax surtax). The rate may be reduced to 0% or 5-25% under a Double Tax Convention, subject to ownership thresholds and beneficial ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the DTA relief, the non-resident payee must submit to the paying Korean entity a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by their home tax authority, covering the calendar year of the income payment. Additionally, the payee must complete Form 21 (Application for Exemption from or Reduction of the Korean Withholding Tax) or Form 23 (Application for the Application of the Treaty Non-Taxation of Income) and file it with the local tax office before payment or, in some cases, before the end of the calendar year following the payment. The tax authority requires the beneficial owner to submit a sworn declaration detailing the income's ownership chain, financial capacity, business substance, and lack of conduit arrangements. If the TRC is not submitted by the payment date, the payer must withhold the full statutory rate; refund procedures are available through an amended return or claim filed within 5 years. For dividends, ownership thresholds under the relevant DTA must be met (e.g., 10% capital ownership or higher per treaty). The tax authority may deny treaty relief where the sole purpose of the transaction is to obtain treaty benefits, per General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the Principal Purpose Test contained in the BEPS MLI.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT 22% (20% CIT + 2% local tax); treaty rates often 5% or 10% (e.g., under the US-Korea treaty 10%; Japan-Korea 10%) for royalties. Interest: statutory WHT 22%; treaty rates generally 10% (e.g., under the US-Korea treaty 10% for most interest; 5% for interest paid to a financial institution). For interest and royalties, the beneficial ownership test and TRC must be verified. Interest paid by a Korean subsidiary to a foreign parent that is deemed debt-equity thin capitalization equity (debt-to-equity ratio exceeding 2:1, or 3:1 for financial institutions) is reclassified as dividends, triggering the 22% dividend WHT. Royalties paid to a foreign related party in excess of arm's length are disallowed as deductions and treated as constructive dividends subject to WHT. Non-resident taxpayers must also file a withholding tax return (Form 25) for any income they pay to other non-residents from Korean sources, e.g., a foreign SaaS vendor paying another foreign vendor for development services used in Korea.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: In South Korea, a Local File must be prepared if the aggregate amount of intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceeds KRW 5 billion during the fiscal year. A Master File is required if the aggregate intercompany transactions exceed KRW 50 billion, or if the revenue of the multinational group exceeds KRW 100 billion and its aggregate intercompany transactions exceed KRW 5 billion. A Country-by-Country report is required if the consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion. Even if statutory thresholds are not met, the National Tax Service may demand contemporaneous documentation for any transaction that is individually above KRW 200 million in monetary value.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Doctrine in South Korea is embedded in the arm's length principle and the anti-abuse provisions of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination. Article 4 of the Act permits the tax authority to disregard transactions lacking economic substance. For software and payroll automation companies, intangible related revenue and intercompany services must be supported by actual business substance, including personnel, office facilities, decision-making autonomy, risk assumption, and the conduct of Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) within Korea. A foreign parent or subsidiary that merely holds contracts and invoices without local substance will be recharacterized, and the income attributable to the Korean site will be taxed in Korea. The National Tax Service may apply upward adjustment based on the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and impose a 10% non-arm's-length penalty, plus compensation tax for unjustified transfer pricing adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully failing to file a corporate income tax return or underreporting Korean-source revenue by hiding digital transactions from the Korean Payroll SaaS platform, settlement revenues, and subscription fees, or deliberately omitting a permanent establishment through sham dependent-agency arrangements that in fact bind the foreign entity to Korean contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 84(1) of the Individual Income Tax Act and Article 166(1) of the Corporate Income Tax Act, intentional false reporting to evade corporate income tax is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 200 million. For evasion exceeding KRW 1 billion, the punishment is imprisonment of up to 7 years. In addition, the tax authority adds a 30% penalty on the underpaid tax plus daily interest. The statute of limitation is 10 years for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in tax evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act Article 167(2) and the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 43. Civil asset restitution requires directors to personally reimburse the evaded tax, penalties, and interest. A criminal conviction is entered on the director's record; the court may issue a stringent condition requiring prison time. Directors with outstanding criminal tax fines or unpaid tax obligations are subject to a travel ban (blacklisting) enforced by the Ministry of Justice, preventing departure from Korea. Persistent non-payment can lead to seizure of personal assets, including bank accounts, shares, and real estate. In serious cases, directors face imprisonment for up to 7 years and fines of up to KRW 300 million for the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating intercompany pricing for software subscription, royalty, or payroll processing services between the Korean entity and its foreign parent or affiliate to shift profits artificially to a low-tax jurisdiction, or failing to prepare and submit the Local File, Master File, and Country-by-Country Report within the statutory thresholds, or maintaining a dummy contract without actual CIGA employees in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 5(2) and Article 11 of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination, tax authority may impose an adjustment to reflect the arm's length price. An additional 10% penalty on the understated tax amount applies (Article 20-2). A separate penalty of KRW 10 million (or KRW 5 million for small-medium enterprises) for non-compliance with documentation submission is set under Article 12(6). The adjustment may also trigger an 20% penalty on foreign related-party transactions if the tax authority determines that the taxpayer refused to cooperate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally sign false transfer pricing declarations or direct the preparation of fabricated intercompany agreements may be charged with fraud under the Korean Penal Code (Article 347) and special tax law violations. If the transfer pricing fraud leads to corporate tax evasion, the director's personal assets can be attached. The National Tax Service may issue a 'Warranty of Collection' against the director's assets. Immovable property and bank accounts are frozen, and the director is placed on the National Tax Service's 'serious delinquent' database, which triggers asset seizure, credit damage, and the revocation of business licenses. Where a director is criminally convicted, the court may order imprisonment of up to 5 years, and a separate order to pay compensation to the tax authority will be levied against the director's estate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean payroll SaaS entity as a pass-through shell with no substantive office, no employees, and no payroll infrastructure; receiving funds through Korean bank accounts while claiming that all payroll services are processed outside Korea; failing to comply with the Financial Transaction Reports Act by not filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) on large or suspicious payroll remittances; or using the corporation to launder proceeds from digital content or gaming market sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 14 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, failure to report a suspicious transaction is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million. The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) may impose fines and order administrative cessation of business. For unregistered financial services, the Electronic Financial Transactions Act Article 49 imposes a 15-year imprisonment maximum. The corporate entity may be dissolved and its tax benefits withdrawn. The National Tax Service may disregard the entity for tax purposes and tax the economic substance in the foreign parent's or beneficial owner's hands.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Legal Entity's directors are personally liable for AML violations under the Specific Financial Information Act and the Commercial Act Article 389(3) if they failed to exercise reasonable oversight. Directors can be held civilly liable for restitution of the full amount laundered and all related taxes. The prosecutor's office can issue a specific travel ban on directors suspected of money laundering, freezing all personal and corporate bank accounts without notice. On conviction, directors face imprisonment of up to 5 years for failing to report STRs, and up to 10 years for money laundering (Article 3 of the Act on Proceeds and Punishment of Crimes). Additionally, the director's directorial disqualification is automatic for 10 years after criminal conviction, and any assets acquired through the crime are subject to confiscation. If the shell company is used to facilitate tax evasion or sanctions evasion, the Commission on Good Administration may blacklist the director and company, barring them from public procurement contracts and banking access across Korea and potentially the EU/US via intelligence sharing.
